avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own means: money from the parks fund, equipment rental, blue-collar worker teams. Variances also allow tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for parks purposes to the purchase of trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, with plant planting, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting sweeper-vacuums, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper to remove abrasives from streets, sidewalks and bike paths. Le Sud-Ouest is accepting a bid of $272,352.78, taxes included, for six sidewalk washers with operators, from April 1, 2026 to May 15, 2028 [CA26 22 0006].

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is entrusting companies with the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six other squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending for one year the snow removal of the Quartier des Spectacles, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord is paying for a grader rented in addition during the season, and Saint-Léonard is drawing $200,000 from its surpluses for staff pay and the purchase of salt and sand, after 39 spreading operations since November 15, 2025, while its budget had planned for 20 [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun is offering to supply the City itself with staff for the snow disposal site.

The City is extending by twelve months the turnkey snow removal contracts of Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, towing contracts in four boroughs, and equipment rental in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Ville-Marie, Anjou and Ahuntsic-Cartierville, for their part, are extending rentals of loader tractors and a grader.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The turnkey snow removal contracts of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.
The turnkey snow removal contract of Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and carrying out work on its water networks: waterworks and sewer pipes, replacement of lead service connections, drinking water production plants and the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. It is awarding contracts for the reconstruction and rehabilitation of pipes on streets in many boroughs. It is also moving forward with the project to disinfect with ozone the wastewater discharged into the Saint-Laurent river.

etapes.texte: The City is raising to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money must be used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen plant.

The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without trenching, redo roadways and sidewalks, and replace lead water service connections. The streets targeted are notably in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, Saint-Laurent, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

The City is retaining Pure Technologies ltd. to install fibre optics and continuously monitor 38 kilometres of prestressed concrete water mains for ten years. City council is taking a step toward a $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks from 2027 to 2031.

aSurveiller.texte: Announced adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary waterworks and sewer networks, on October 19, 2026.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 4 at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant in January 2027, for about six weeks of work.
Completion of the water pipe work on rue de la Cathédrale pushed back to March 2027.
Rue Guy worksite expected to continue until December 2027.
Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant expected in 2029; the contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 are to finish in the last quarter of 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.

etapes.titre: Funding request for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park, with a footbridge about 150 metres long. The project also includes rainwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The conseil d'agglomération approves construction of a greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then assigns its completion to the conseil municipal, which awards it to the arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. In July, the borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. a $499,865.92 contract to supply and install two greenhouses.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a $1,091,693.37 contract for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel. The work includes a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator and a controller to manage biogas capture.

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, cycling facilities and plantings.

Two companies are awarded 30-month contracts for general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park. The City also extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor by five months, for $296,349.21 more; the compost is used, among other things, for landscaping the park.

etapes.titre: Snow removal extended by six months
etapes.texte: The City extends by six months the snow removal contract for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the soccer stadium, awarded to 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky), for $193,215.49 more.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, closes on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work must be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The Boisé Ouest sector, 26 hectares, is to be added in 2027 to the 65 hectares already open to the public.
The snow removal extension covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bulb-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, in the making: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, extra mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work was 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, and was to resume on May 15, 2026, to finish on July 10, 2026.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, by adopting conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 report on listed areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. a contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, for a total expense of $481,850.45. The culvert, damaged by the August 2024 rains, is part of the project to modernize the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub.

The City is giving Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée the job of cutting down ash trees and other dying trees in the Grand parc de l'Ouest, for $1,370,433.02, taxes included, plus contingencies and quantity variation. The file indicates about 9,000 trees to be cut down, from fall 2026 to early summer 2028, to limit emerald ash borer and secure the sites.

Paysagiste Solarco inc. is getting the snow removal of service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, for $178,330.82, taxes included, from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2028. 9232-3914 Québec inc. is getting the janitorial maintenance of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, for a total expense of $704,619.24, from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2030.

aSurveiller.texte: Submission of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.
Start of the snow removal contract on November 1, 2026, until April 30, 2028.
Start of janitorial maintenance of the nine buildings on November 1, 2026, until October 31, 2030, with an option to extend until October 31, 2031.
Tree removal work from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is putting in place a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026 and the value of the unbilled rent for the church is assessed at $57,076.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for winter 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for projects on inclusion, coexistence in public space and awareness. The amounts cover a three-year period ending on December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fitting out of the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social coexistence projects; donors do not choose the project funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fitting-out work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area move toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the litigation over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary layouts.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a piece of land to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking of its agents' vehicles, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring piece of land to a company for paid parking reserved for members of an app.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work involves sewers, waterworks, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: Main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, waterworks, roadway, electrical network and lighting in the eco-district, as well as for environmental soil management. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est site.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, followed by the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 housing units per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the land rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the land for growing sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the community garden land continues until December 31, 2027.
The land at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for programming activities from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

The work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street-naming file indicates that the site's layout is expected around 2032 and that four other public places still need to be named.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collection, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, areas and frequency of collection in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste treatment contracts and its contracts related to ecocentres, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the 2025 report on the agglomeration's residual materials management.

etapes.texte: The City is extending its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, by six months each time, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and Moose Creek, Ontario, while waiting for the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre to come into service.

etapes.titre: Bin purchases and sorting equipment loans
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to provide collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration extends the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-buried containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, assigns two firms to conduct studies on buildings located on former waste disposal sites, and extends the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program to loan dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The dumping authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former hippodrome Blue Bonnets: sale of land, loan by-laws, water supply system in the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former hippodrome, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained from the Québec government a new deadline to sell a first piece of land, adopted loan by-laws for the development of public land and for water mains in the Namur–De la Savane sector, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. It is also leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: New deadline to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former hippodrome, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not involve any financial compensation and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan for the development of public land in the Quartier Namur-Hippodrome: soil remediation, sewers and water supply, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. The urban agglomeration council adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella.

etapes.titre: Real estate project at 7301, boulevard Décarie
etapes.texte: The borough adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, one of which is to house a municipal sports and leisure centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities in the sector, and the borough secretary will hold a public consultation meeting.

The City leases parcels of the site to three organizations for $100 or $200 in rent: temporary urban agriculture with MultiCaf and with Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora, and a transitional nursery with Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain. Each lease specifies the real estate subsidy represented by the gap with the rental value.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: new deadline granted to the City to sell a first piece of land on the site.
April 30, 2027: end of the urban agriculture lease with MultiCaf.
March 31, 2028: end of the extended lease with Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora. April 30, 2028: end of the transitional nursery lease with Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain.
2031: deadline for completing infrastructure set as a condition for the federal subsidy mentioned in the loan by-laws.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and renovation of parks in several boroughs: new water play areas, playgrounds, dog parks, sports fields and trails. It is also adjusting several contracts already awarded, notably for contaminated soil. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is having walls and a culvert repaired, submitting an application for a dark-sky designation, and awarding maintenance contracts.

etapes.texte: The City entrusts the winning team of an architecture competition with the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It also pays money to Verdun for environmental and geotechnical studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, and the Sud-Ouest borough signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec for phase 4 of parc d'Argenson.

etapes.titre: Grand parc de l'Ouest: work and protection
etapes.texte: The City adds $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild the culvert under this road, at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and lists the Anse-à-l'Orme sector in the directory of protected natural areas.

Several contracts already awarded are amended: construction monitoring for parc du Bassin-à-Bois, work at parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, professional services for parc Percy-Walters and for parc Denise-Morelle, and additional contingencies for parc Villeray.

etapes.titre: New construction sites and land changes
etapes.texte: Contracts are awarded to redevelop parcs Denise-Morelle, J.O.R.-Leduc and Baldwin, and the City pays for the decontamination of parc George-Vernot. It also converts a street section at parc Campbell Ouest into a local park, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension requests the same change for a 75.2-square-metre strip of laneway at parc Le Prévost.

etapes.titre: Maintenance of the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City awards three contracts: snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, the felling of ash trees and dying trees, and janitorial maintenance of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner selected in October 2026, contract in December 2026 and installation of the artwork in 2028.
The change of status of a strip of laneway at parc Le Prévost must be adopted by the executive committee on October 7, 2026 and by city council on October 19, 2026.
Cap-Saint-Jacques application: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance by April 2032.

Grand parc de l'Ouest maintenance contracts: snow removal from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028; janitorial maintenance from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: end of construction in June 2026 and final acceptance of the work in June 2027.
Work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc from August 2026 to June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial activity by-laws.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and overseeing temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the by-laws that close the streets and allow terraces, sales and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot, and official name.

etapes.titre: Grant rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided the council closes the street by by-law [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee distributes $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

etapes.titre: Money paid to commercial development corporations
etapes.texte: The boroughs pay contributions to the commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite" [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The by-law on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract for avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of heritage buildings of interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people in residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public assembly was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation took place from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevards Crémazie and Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for certain work in the designated heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on building demolition, after a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève indicates it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks have been announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood police stations, city council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a sergeant-detective to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, for three years starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys 11 patrol motorcycles, extends janitorial services at headquarters by one year, and awards work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It also awards a contract for meals for detained persons and extends maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

etapes.titre: Leases for neighbourhood police stations and premises
etapes.texte: The City leases 50 parking spaces at 260 boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles. It renews the leases for the training centre in Anjou, neighbourhood police station 15 in Verdun, and neighbourhood police station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights.

The City enters into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police shooting training, and extends the SPVM's mail pickup and distribution service by one year. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in the department's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" fundraising day at neighbourhood police station 46, on October 23, 2026; the Anjou borough buys 62 tickets.
The port patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, begins February 1, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, Alcool, Cannabis and ACCEF committees are extended until March 31, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: The City approves the 2026 budget and the 2026-2035 capital works program of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then a series of STM loan by-laws for its buses, its metro and its buildings. It sells or lends land to the STM to expand metro facilities, and signs agreements to carry out municipal work at the same time as public transit work. Borough councils also adopt motions on future public transit projects.

etapes.titre: STM budget, fuel and leased land
etapes.texte: Elected officials approve the STM's 2026 budget and 2026-2035 capital works program, and conclude a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply diesel. The City also renews the lease to the STM of a 2,787 square-metre lot in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, used as a parking lot for its agents' vehicles.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29, taxes included. It also signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the metro ventilation station, avenue Wiseman, in Outremont, and purchases advertising space in the metro and buses for Espace pour la vie.

Elected officials approve STM loans for bus priority measures, the repair of metro and surface infrastructure, cybersecurity, the extension of the service life of MR-73 cars and the analysis of their replacement. Each approval amends the 2026-2035 Capital Works Program.

Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and restore the tunnel vault of the green line between Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent, 24 hours a day, from June 10 to July 31, 2026. The City does not oppose the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM, pays $382,000 to the STM for the 2026 UCI Road World Championships and adds $250,000 to the integrated worksite at Berri-UQAM station.

The City entrusts Artelia Canada and Stantec Experts-conseils with professional services for the redevelopment of the blue line corridor, from Jean-Talon Est to Anjou. Councils adopt motions on preserving the tunnel boring machine "Lisette", on a structuring project in the East of Montréal and on a structuring project in the Grand Sud-Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the Ahuntsic-Cartierville parking lot runs for three years starting October 1, 2026, for a maximum of 92 days per year.
According to the blue line file, contracts must be awarded in August and October 2026, metro work must take place from 2026 to 2030 and stations must open in 2031.
Work at the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, must continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; work is planned from June 2026 to March 2028.
The agreements for the redevelopment of the blue line corridor cover 72 months, from October 2026 to October 2032, with a possible 12-month extension.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the BIXI bike-share system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI bike-share system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new cycling projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an order that makes official the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse, and requires mandatory manoeuvres for drivers up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives to be spread notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved that Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carry out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville hired Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bicycles, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then hired Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers that serve as the base for the stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the submission of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
